prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Charlotte for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t a single objectively “best” lawyer for every car-accident case — the right lawyer depends on the facts of your crash, the injuries, whether liability is clear, and your goals (quick settlement vs trial). I can help you find and evaluate the best lawyer for your situation.

How to find the best personal-injury lawyer in Charlotte for your car-accident case
- Use reputable directories and vet credentials
  - North Carolina State Bar (verify license and disciplinary history).
  - Lawyer-rating sites: Super Lawyers, Martindale‑Hubbell (AV ratings), Avvo, Google/Yelp reviews.
  - Local referrals: friends/family, other attorneys, or the Mecklenburg County Bar referral service.

- Look for these important qualifications
  - Substantial personal-injury/car-accident experience (years and % of practice).
  - Trial experience and courtroom results (jury verdicts and settlements).
  - Track record with similar injuries and with the at-fault insurer.
  - Good communication: responsive and clear about strategy.
  - Works on contingency (no fee unless you recover) and clear fee/cost policy.
  - Team support — paralegals and investigators to handle evidence and medical records.

- Questions to ask in a free consultation
  - How many car-accident cases have you handled? How many went to trial?
  - What percentage of your practice is auto/personal injury?
  - Who will handle my case day-to-day?
  - What’s your contingency fee and what costs am I responsible for?
  - What’s your assessment of my case and a realistic settlement range/timeline?
  - Any conflicts, disciplinary history, or malpractice claims?

Practical next steps you can take now
- Preserve evidence: photos of vehicles/scene, witness contact info, traffic-camera or dashcam footage if any.
- Get and keep all medical records and bills.
- Obtain the police report and your insurer’s claim number.
- Don’t give recorded statements to the other driver’s insurer without talking to a lawyer first.
- Be mindful of North Carolina deadlines: generally 3 years from the injury for personal injury suits (N.C. Gen. Stat. §1‑52(16)), so don’t delay legal review.

If you want, I can:
- Draft a short phone script/email to contact multiple Charlotte attorneys.
- Create a shortlist of well-reviewed Charlotte personal-injury lawyers (I’ll need permission to look up current local listings or you can provide favorites you’ve found and I’ll help evaluate them).
- Walk through what to bring to your consultations and help compare responses.

Tell me: do you want me to draft a contact script, or would you like me to build a shortlist of lawyers in Charlotte (I’ll need permission to search the web)? Also, brief details about the crash (date, injuries, whether fault was disputed) will help me tailor advice.
